briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Operators Find Workarounds as Rescheduling and Psychedelics Momentum Builds Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan dispensaries are opening new storefronts, striking supplier cost-share deals, and pushing back on the 24% wholesale tax through the courts and this fall's governor's race, giving operators real paths forward despite the levy's bite. Nationally, DEA has formally argued for Schedule III in its post-hearing brief while MSO stocks hit 2026 highs and Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy races toward what could be the first FDA-approved psychedelic drug.

local.text: Michigan-based Lume Cannabis Co. opened a new Ann Arbor storefront at 2247 W. Liberty Street, with a three-day grand opening event — fresh proof that operators are still expanding footprint in the state's toughest tax environment yet.

U.P. chain Rize, which operates three Upper Michigan locations, has kept growing by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers — splitting the 24% wholesale tax burden instead of absorbing it alone, a playbook other operators can copy.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary is targeting a fall opening for a dispensary paired with a full-service restaurant, pushing the hospitality-forward retail format further than most Michigan dispensaries have gone.

Jars Cannabis notched a win in Madison Heights after staff blocked a police Flock license-plate camera stationed near the store, forcing its removal — a small but symbolic operator victory against surveillance overreach.

Relief may be coming regardless of who wins in November: GOP nominee John James is pledging to roll back the 24% wholesale tax as part of his "Freedom Agenda," while MiCIA's original court challenge to the levy is now headed to trial this month.

national.text: DEA formally argued in its final post-hearing brief that marijuana no longer meets Schedule I criteria and should move to Schedule III — the clearest signal yet that federal rescheduling is advancing toward a real rule change.

Curaleaf is pushing a cross-border consolidation play with a $4-per-share, 45% premium takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis that would create $1.5 billion-plus in combined pro forma revenue and add over 50 tons of EU-GMP cultivation capacity.

Cannabis capital markets are heating up: the MSOS ETF hit a 2026 high ahead of the DEA hearing, Trulieve began trading on the NYSE, and Cresco Labs landed a $50 million revolving credit facility it says will fund acquisitions and support a future senior-exchange uplisting.

Well-capitalized operators are turning distress into growth — Cresco just paid $50 million for nine PharmaCann medical dispensaries in Pennsylvania, the country's second-largest MMJ market, as struggling MSOs sell off assets.

Compass Pathways just landed an FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher and rolling NDA review for its psilocybin therapy COMP360, positioning it to become the first approved psychedelic drug as the FDA also finalized clinical-trial guidance and set a September 14 public hearing on therapeutic psychedelic use.
